content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Ebooks online

Conventional platforms like Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle promise simplicity but deliver dependency. They handle hosting, payments, and delivery—until they don’t. Your store runs on their servers, your payments route through their processors, and your files sit in their storage. This works until your country is flagged, your account is suspended, or their fees rise. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is different: it deploys a self-owned stack using GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. Payments are processed via NOWPayments, which supports 300+ cryptocurrencies with a flat 0.5% fee. You own every component. No platform can shut you down. No geography can exclude you. This is infrastructure sovereignty—not a workaround, but a permanent architecture.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Conventional platforms exclude countries based on financial risk models, not technical limitations. Nigeria, Zimbabwe, and Venezuela are routinely blocked because Stripe and PayPal prioritize compliance over access. Even if a platform claims to support your region, payment processors often decline transactions from these locations. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack bypasses this entirely by using on-chain crypto payments. NOWPayments verifies transactions directly on the blockchain, requiring no buyer account or KYC. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON keep fees under $0.10 per transaction. This isn’t a hack—it’s base-layer infrastructure built for regions where conventional systems fail. The stack is deployed in your name, on your domains, with no third-party dependencies. Geography becomes irrelevant when your commerce stack is sovereign.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Conventional platforms charge 5-10% per transaction, plus monthly fees for advanced features. Payments settle in 2-7 days, and chargebacks can freeze your account. Crypto payments via NOWPayments settle the moment the transaction confirms on-chain—often in minutes. The 0.5% fee is fixed, with no hidden costs. While crypto volatility is a concern, stablecoins like USDT or USDC eliminate this risk. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack integrates stablecoin support by default, ensuring predictable revenue. The $197 deployment fee is a one-time cost, not a subscription. You own the stack afterward, with no ongoing fees to COREMERCH or any platform. This model isn’t cheaper—it’s structurally different, designed for creators who prioritize ownership over convenience.
Conventional platforms exclude you based on geography, not capability.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

On conventional platforms, your store, data, and files belong to the platform. They control access, and their terms dictate how you operate. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack gives you full ownership. Your store is hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, your orders are stored in Supabase or Google Sheets, and your files are delivered via Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive. Automation is handled by Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, ensuring instant product delivery the moment payment is verified. The stack is deployed in your name, with no COREMERCH access after delivery. This isn’t just a store—it’s a self-owned commerce infrastructure. You decide how it operates, scales, and evolves. No platform can dictate your terms.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you’re in a region where Stripe and PayPal are unavailable, conventional platforms are not an option—they’re a dead end. Workarounds like using a VPN or proxying payments through a friend’s account are temporary and risky. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack is the only permanent solution. It’s built for creators who need infrastructure sovereignty, not platform dependency. If you’re selling ebooks, courses, or digital products and want full ownership, automatic delivery, and geo-agnostic payments, this stack is your architecture. The $197 deployment fee is an investment in ownership, not a cost of convenience. Choose this if you’re done with workarounds and ready to build on infrastructure you control.
